trace.code: rfc3966_domainlabel_(StrCat("[", alphanum_, "]+((\\-)*[", alphanum_, "])*")), rfc3966_toplabel_(StrCat("[", kValidAlphaInclUppercase, "]+((\\-)*[", alphanum_, "])*"))

preconditions: Victim application calls the libphonenumber C++ parser (PhoneNumberUtil::Parse / ParseAndKeepRawInput / any isValidNumber-style wrapper that routes through Parse) on attacker-controlled strings, as virtually every signup, SMS and phone-number-validation service does
The C++ library is built with its default regex backend, ICU (USE_ICU_REGEXP=ON is the CMake default)
Attacker supplies a tel: URI whose phone-context parameter is a long sequence of ambiguous domain labels failing at the end, e.g. tel:253-0000;phone-context=(aa.){30}aa!

evidence.vulnerable_version: all releases through v9.0.43 (86ea33c, 2026-11-04) and every earlier release
evidence.observed_result: With the real ICU adapter + the v9.0.43 domainname pattern, FullMatch on (aa.){N}aa! grows exponentially: 0.6 ms (N=6), 5.3 ms (N=8), 96.6 ms (N=10), 597.9 ms (N=12), 6114.2 ms (N=14), and N=30 is still inside the matcher after 15000 ms (child killed). The upstream-fixed pattern rejects the same N=30 input in 0.015 ms.

real_exploit.backend: real project source: regexp_adapter_icu.cc + string_byte_sink.cc + default_logger.cc + logger.cc vendored verbatim from v9.0.43, compiled with zig cc against the ICU 78 regex engine that libphonenumber uses by default; the two pattern strings are reconstructed verbatim from phonenumberutil.cc:793-795 (vulnerable) and upstream commit 981600c (fixed)
real_exploit.demonstrated: PhoneNumberUtil::IsPhoneContextValid() feeds the attacker-controlled phone-context of a tel: URI to rfc3966_domainname_pattern_->FullMatch(). With the v9.0.43 pattern the real ICU adapter exhibits exponential backtracking: N=30 labels keeps a worker thread inside FullMatch beyond 15 s, while the fixed pattern rejects the identical input in 0.015 ms. A single request therefore pins a server thread indefinitely; a handful of requests exhausts a worker pool.
